title: Scoliosis Screening and Limb Alignment — Adams Test, Knees and Feet

hook.en: A child's curved spine, knocked knees or flat feet are often normal for the age — and sometimes the first sign of something that needs a specialist. Learn what is normal, what to measure and when to refer.
hook.ur: Bachay ki mudi hui spine, knock knees ya flat feet aksar umar ke hisaab se normal hain — aur kabhi kabhi us cheez ki pehli nishani jis ko specialist chahiye. Seekhein normal kya hai, kya naapna hai aur kab refer karna hai.

goal.en: By the end, you'll screen for scoliosis with the forward-bend (Adams) test and a scoliometer, recognise genu valgum, varum and recurvatum and pes planus and cavus, and know the red flags that need referral.
goal.ur: End tak aap forward-bend (Adams) test aur scoliometer se scoliosis screen karenge, genu valgum, varum aur recurvatum aur pes planus aur cavus pehchanenge, aur woh red flags jaanenge jin par referral zaroori hai.

text.en: **Scoliosis** is a sideways curve of the spine **with rotation**: one shoulder and one scapula sit higher, the waist creases are uneven and, in forward bending, a **rib hump** appears on the convex side. The **Adams forward-bend test** (with a scoliometer on the apex) screens for it: a trunk rotation of about **5–7° or more** warrants referral for X-ray. In the limbs, children pass through normal phases (bow legs as toddlers, knock knees at 3–6 years, flat feet until about age 6–8), so context and age matter.
text.ur: **Scoliosis** spine ka side ki taraf curve hai **rotation ke saath**: ek shoulder aur ek scapula unchi, waist creases barabar nahi aur aage jhukne par convex side par **rib hump** nazar aata hai. **Adams forward-bend test** (apex par scoliometer ke saath) isay screen karta hai: takriban **5–7° ya zyada** trunk rotation X-ray ke liye referral chahti hai. Limbs mein bachay normal marhalon se guzarte hain (toddlers mein bow legs, 3–6 saal mein knock knees, takriban 6–8 saal tak flat feet), is liye context aur umar ahem hain.

text.en: Think of a bent garden hose twisted as it curves: you cannot see the twist from the front but if you look along the hose it rises like a hump on one side. That is the rib hump seen when the child bends forward: the twist (rotation) of the spine pushes the ribs out on one side.
text.ur: Mori hui bagh ki hose ka tasawwur karein jo mur'ti hui twist bhi hoti hai: samne se twist nazar nahi aata lekin hose ke saath dekhein to ek taraf hump ki tarah uthta hai. Yeh woh rib hump hai jo bachay ke aage jhukne par nazar aata hai: spine ka twist (rotation) ek taraf ribs ko bahar dhakelta hai.

intro.en: One shoulder and scapula sit higher and the waist creases are uneven. Watch the loop and imagine the child bending forward: the convex side shows a **rib hump**. Check the curve with the forward-bend test; refer curves of 20° or more, any painful curve and any that is progressing quickly.
intro.ur: Ek shoulder aur scapula unchi aur waist creases barabar nahi. Loop dekhein aur tasawwur karein ke bacha aage jhuk raha hai: convex side par **rib hump** nazar aata hai. Forward-bend test se curve check karein; 20° ya zyada, har dardnak curve aur tezi se barhne wale curve ko refer karein.

question.en: A 12-year-old girl has a rib hump on forward bending and a scoliometer reading of 8°. What next?
question.ur: 12 saal ki bachi ko aage jhukne par rib hump hai aur scoliometer reading 8° hai. Aage kya?

text.en: Refer for a standing spinal X-ray (a reading of about 5–7° or more)
text.ur: Standing spinal X-ray ke liye refer karein (takriban 5–7° ya zyada reading)

feedback.en: Yes — the scoliometer screens; the X-ray measures the Cobb angle that decides observation, bracing or surgery.
feedback.ur: Haan — scoliometer screen karta hai; X-ray Cobb angle naapta hai jo observation, bracing ya surgery ka faisla karta hai.

text.en: Reassure her it is posture and discharge
text.ur: Tasalli de kar discharge karein ke posture hai

feedback.en: A structural curve does not correct with posture; do not dismiss it.
feedback.ur: Structural curve posture se theek nahi hoti; isay nazar-andaz na karein.

feedback.en: Treatment depends on the Cobb angle and progression, not stretching alone.
feedback.ur: Ilaaj Cobb angle aur progression par depend karta hai, sirf stretching par nahi.

intro.en: The knees angle toward each other and the ankles stay apart (the intermalleolar distance widens). It is normal in 3–6 year olds; persistent or asymmetrical deformity loads the lateral knee and can overstretch the medial collateral structures.
intro.ur: Knees ek doosre ki taraf jhukte hain aur ankles door rehte hain (intermalleolar distance barh jati hai). 3–6 saal ke bachon mein normal; mustaqil ya asymmetrical deformity lateral knee par bojh daalti hai aur medial collateral structures ko overstretch kar sakti hai.

intro.en: The medial arch collapses and the heel tilts outwards. Flexible flat foot (the arch returns on tiptoe) is usually painless and normal; a **rigid** flat foot needs assessment. Check the "too many toes" sign from behind and the navicular drop.
intro.ur: Medial arch gir jati hai aur heel bahar ki taraf tilt hoti hai. Flexible flat foot (tiptoe par arch wapas aati hai) aam taur par dard-rahit aur normal; **rigid** flat foot ka assessment zaroori hai. Peechay se “too many toes” sign aur navicular drop check karein.

rows.en: In toddlers, improving by about 2 years
rows.ur: Toddlers mein, takriban 2 saal tak behtar hota hua

rows.en: Persisting beyond 3 years, asymmetrical, progressive or with short stature (rickets, Blount disease)
rows.ur: 3 saal ke baad bhi rehna, asymmetrical, barhta hua ya chhote qad ke saath (rickets, Blount disease)
3–6 saal mein, barhne ke saath theek hota hua

rows.en: Intermalleolar distance over about 8–10 cm, asymmetrical, painful or progressing
rows.ur: Intermalleolar distance takriban 8–10 cm se zyada, asymmetrical, dardnak ya barhta hua

rows.en: In hypermobile people with good control
rows.ur: Hypermobile logon mein jin ka control acha ho

rows.en: With quadriceps or hamstring weakness, drop foot or knee pain (it stretches the posterior capsule)
rows.ur: Quadriceps ya hamstring ki kamzori, drop foot ya knee pain ke saath (yeh posterior capsule ko stretch karta hai)

rows.en: Flexible, painless, arch returns on tiptoe, in children and many adults
rows.ur: Flexible, dard-rahit, tiptoe par arch wapas, bachon aur bohat se bado mein

rows.en: Rigid, painful, unilateral, or with tibialis posterior dysfunction
rows.ur: Rigid, dardnak, ek taraf ya tibialis posterior dysfunction ke saath
Normal variant ke taur par kam

rows.en: Often neurological (Charcot–Marie–Tooth): claw toes, recurrent ankle sprains, rigid foot
rows.ur: Aksar neurological (Charcot–Marie–Tooth): claw toes, baar baar ankle sprains, rigid foot

text.en: **Over-treating normal development and under-reacting to red flags.** Do not put orthoses on every flexible flat foot or splint every toddler's bowed legs: these are normal and most resolve. But do not reassure a painful, rigid, asymmetrical or progressing deformity, and never forget the **neurological screen** for a high-arched foot (reflexes, sensation, power, family history). When unsure, measure, photograph and review in a few months.
text.ur: **Normal nashonuma ka zyada ilaaj aur red flags par kam ardaab.** Har flexible flat foot par orthoses na lagayein aur har toddler ki bowed legs par splint na karein: yeh normal hain aur zyada tar theek ho jati hain. Lekin dardnak, rigid, asymmetrical ya barhti deformity ko tasalli na dein, aur high-arched foot ke liye **neurological screen** (reflexes, sensation, power, khandani history) kabhi na bhoolein. Shak ho to naapein, photograph lein aur chand mahine baad dobara dekhein.

question.en: Which finding in a high-arched (cavus) foot should trigger a neurological referral?
question.ur: High-arched (cavus) foot mein kaun si finding neurological referral ka sabab honi chahiye?

text.en: Claw toes with recurrent ankle sprains, a rigid foot and reduced ankle reflexes (consider Charcot–Marie–Tooth)
text.ur: Claw toes, baar baar ankle sprains, rigid foot aur kam ankle reflexes (Charcot–Marie–Tooth par ghor)

feedback.en: Yes — a cavus foot with progressive weakness and reduced reflexes suggests a hereditary neuropathy.
feedback.ur: Haan — barhti kamzori aur kam reflexes ke saath cavus foot hereditary neuropathy ka ishara hai.

text.en: A mild, symmetrical high arch in an athlete with no symptoms
text.ur: Athlete mein halka, symmetrical high arch jis ko koi symptoms nahi

feedback.en: A symmetrical, painless, flexible high arch can be a normal variant.
feedback.ur: Symmetrical, dard-rahit, flexible high arch normal variant ho sakta hai.

text.en: A flexible flat foot that is painless
text.ur: Flexible flat foot jo dard-rahit hai

text.en: **Measure and monitor.** For scoliosis: record shoulder and waist symmetry, the scoliometer angle at the apex and the rib hump height; schedule review every 4–6 months in a growing child and refer for any rise of 5° or more. For knees: measure the intermalleolar distance (valgus) or the intercondylar distance (varus) with the ankles or knees touching. For feet: measure the navicular drop (a drop of more than about 10 mm is excessive pronation) and check whether the arch re-forms on tiptoe and on big-toe extension (the windlass test).
text.ur: **Naapein aur monitor karein.** Scoliosis ke liye: shoulder aur waist ki symmetry, apex par scoliometer angle aur rib hump ki unchai likhein; barhte bachay mein har 4–6 mahine baad review lagayein aur 5° ya zyada izafe par refer karein. Knees ke liye: ankles ya knees milane par intermalleolar distance (valgus) ya intercondylar distance (varus) naapein. Feet ke liye: navicular drop naapein (takriban 10 mm se zyada drop excessive pronation hai) aur dekhein ke arch tiptoe par aur big-toe extension (windlass test) par dobara bante hain ya nahi.

question.en: Why is a painful scoliosis a red flag even if the curve is small?
question.ur: Chhoti curve ho tab bhi dardnak scoliosis red flag kyun hai?

answer.en: Idiopathic adolescent scoliosis is usually **painless**. Pain suggests another cause: a tumour (osteoid osteoma, spinal cord tumour), infection, a disc problem or spondylolysis. Any painful, rapidly progressing or atypical curve (left thoracic curve, abnormal neurology) needs medical review and often an MRI.
answer.ur: Idiopathic adolescent scoliosis aam taur par **dard-rahit** hoti hai. Dard kisi aur wajah ki taraf ishara karta hai: tumour (osteoid osteoma, spinal cord tumour), infection, disc ka masla ya spondylolysis. Har dardnak, tezi se barhti ya ghair-mamooli curve (left thoracic curve, ghair-mamooli neurology) ko medical review aur aksar MRI chahiye.

question.en: What does the "too many toes" sign suggest when seen from behind?
question.ur: Peechay se dikhne wala “too many toes” sign kya batata hai?

text.en: A collapsed medial arch with the heel tilted outward (pes planus / pronation)
text.ur: Gira hua medial arch aur heel bahar ki taraf tilted (pes planus / pronation)

feedback.en: Yes — more toes are visible lateral to the heel because the forefoot has abducted and the heel has valgused.
feedback.ur: Haan — heel ke bahar zyada toes nazar aati hain kyunke forefoot abduct aur heel valgus ho gayi hai.

feedback.en: Normal feet show only one to two toes.
feedback.ur: Normal pairon mein sirf ek se do toes nazar aati hain.

feedback.en: That is a knee hyperextension finding.
feedback.ur: Yeh knee hyperextension ki finding hai.

text.en: **Refer promptly** for a child with scoliosis who has pain, a rapidly increasing curve, abnormal neurology (weakness, reflex change, bladder or bowel symptoms) or a left thoracic curve; for bowed legs that are asymmetric or progressing beyond age 3; and for any child with a limp and hip or knee pain (slipped capital femoral epiphysis, infection). Do not treat spinal deformity in a growing child with manipulation.
text.ur: **Foran refer karein** scoliosis wale bachay ko jis ko dard ho, curve tezi se barh rahi ho, ghair-mamooli neurology (kamzori, reflex ki tabdeeli, bladder ya bowel symptoms) ho ya left thoracic curve ho; asymmetric ya 3 saal ke baad barhti bowed legs; aur har bachay ko jis ko langdana aur hip ya knee ka dard ho (slipped capital femoral epiphysis, infection). Barhte bachay ki spinal deformity ko manipulation se treat na karein.

summary.en: Scoliosis is a curve with rotation: screen with the Adams forward-bend test and a scoliometer (about 5–7° or more needs an X-ray).
summary.ur: Scoliosis rotation ke saath curve hai: Adams forward-bend test aur scoliometer se screen karein (takriban 5–7° ya zyada X-ray chahiye).

summary.en: Many limb alignments are normal for age (bow legs, knock knees, flexible flat feet); worry about rigid, painful, asymmetrical or progressing ones and cavus feet.
summary.ur: Bohat si limb alignments umar ke hisaab se normal hain (bow legs, knock knees, flexible flat feet); rigid, dardnak, asymmetrical ya barhti hui aur cavus feet ki fikar karein.

summary.en: A painful scoliosis, abnormal neurology or a progressing curve needs prompt referral; measure, photograph and review over time.
summary.ur: Dardnak scoliosis, ghair-mamooli neurology ya barhti curve ko foran referral chahiye; naapein, photograph lein aur waqt ke saath review karein.

front.en: What is the Adams forward-bend test for?
front.ur: Adams forward-bend test kis liye hai?

back.en: Screening for structural scoliosis: a rib hump or scoliometer trunk rotation of about 5–7° or more.
back.ur: Structural scoliosis ki screening: rib hump ya takriban 5–7° ya zyada scoliometer trunk rotation.

back.en: At about 3–6 years, correcting with growth.
back.ur: Takriban 3–6 saal mein, barhne ke saath theek hote hue.

front.en: What distinguishes flexible from rigid flat foot?
front.ur: Flexible aur rigid flat foot mein kya farq hai?

back.en: The arch re-forms on tiptoe (or big-toe extension) in a flexible foot; it does not in a rigid one.
back.ur: Flexible foot mein tiptoe (ya big-toe extension) par arch dobara banti hai; rigid mein nahi.

front.en: A cavus foot with claw toes and reduced ankle jerks suggests?
front.ur: Cavus foot, claw toes aur kam ankle jerks kya batate hain?

back.en: A neurological cause such as Charcot–Marie–Tooth disease.
